target.title: fix(slack): prevent duplicate reply controls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Slack users could see the same approval, button, or select row twice when a reply supplied both the canonical portable presentation and its deprecated interactive mirror.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack now uses one shared merge path for ordinary replies, outbound sends and block budgeting, and message-action sends. It renders deprecated interactive controls after native offsets, then subtracts only exact OpenClaw-generated mirrors as a multiset; raw Slack blocks, intentional repeated presentation rows, surplus legacy rows, and controls with different labels, values, URLs, styles, placeholders, or options remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Mirrored Slack controls render once and keep unique Block Kit IDs. Intentionally repeated or meaningfully different controls still render independently.

## Evidence

- Before/after regressions cover exact mirrored buttons and selects, authored repeated rows, surplus legacy rows, semantic differences, reconstructed key order, message-action sends, final outbound delivery, and the 50-block budget boundary.
- Sanitized exact-head AWS Crabbox `run_c4c6e35742ac`: 3 Slack test files passed, 75/75 tests.
- Sanitized exact-head AWS Crabbox `run_605d0989658a`: full `pnpm check:changed` passed, including extension/test typechecks, changed-file lint, import-cycle and architecture guards, attribution, and dependency checks.
- Fresh autoreview: no actionable findings; final lint correction reviewed clean at 0.94 confidence.
- Hosted CI is green at `1d4560ce4c5f7b04c1e0a93e71227c446a64cbd9` apart from the evidence-policy check this section satisfies.
